securityPolicy: Resolved policy for staticAssets.ts and supporting fastRefreshCompiler.ts: no inherited SECURITY.md content. Existing scoped threat model applies.
conclusion: No new plausible trust-boundary vulnerability identified in the final diff. The helper removes repeated whole-artifact copies, and the reserved refresh manifest is rewritten as data with compiler bootstrap consistency enforced. Existing source/module and network authority controls remain in the call path.

evidence.detail: rewriteJavaScript only parses source and collects string-literal spans; it does not evaluate uploaded/generated code. Existing URL selection semantics and binary fetch sink are retained. The early HTTPS text filter can skip work but grants no new execution or network capability.

StringLiteral nodes are leaves; TypeScript source traversal produces ordered disjoint ranges. Each range is replaced once using JSON.stringify of a local digest path, preserving JavaScript string boundaries.

Unique URLs are processed in fixed concurrency batches through fetchAsset. Cache, count/byte limits, DNS/IP validation, redirects, MIME/magic checks and current-authority checks at lines73-100 apply equally to URLs newly discovered in manifest code.

Single forward chunks array plus one join replaces the reverse-loop full-artifact copy per literal. Total rewrite assembly scales with original source and replacement output size, without repeating the entire artifact for each repeated literal.
Only the fixed /_wcb/refresh.json artifact is interpreted. It is emitted by fastRefreshCompiler.ts:102; uploaded public paths cannot replace reserved _wcb artifacts (isolatedPreview.ts:205).

Manifest input requires application/json, at most 24 MiB, version1, string entry, object/nonarray modules with at most2000 members. Every code value must be a string of at most2 MiB (line152). JSON.parse creates data; no custom reviver/getter or host code execution is involved. Invalid/null shapes throw into the existing cleanup path.

Only module.code changes. Module IDs, entry, imports, boundary and propagate metadata are retained. Compiler generates IDs/import maps from the admitted bundle graph at fastRefreshCompiler.ts:55-66,93; runtime localRequire authority remains unchanged at its line98.

Original canonical JSON must appear in the exact compiler marker let manifest=...;const cache= exactly once. The compiler emits that same marker at fastRefreshCompiler.ts:97. Missing/multiple markers refuse publication. Replacement is one slice/join operation over the compiler-owned app artifact.

The same serialized updated manifest is written to both bootstrap and refresh.json. Parsed manifest objects and new Buffers are placed into the copied files map (line70); original build buffers/source bytes are not mutated.

Remaining artifact traversal uses the updated map snapshot, so it preserves the replaced bootstrap. Newly inserted binary artifacts have verified inert MIME types and do not introduce executable source.

Final current-authority/deadline check and snapshot limits (line179) still guard return. Changes do not introduce an alternate output or fetch bypass; finally at line184 retains cancellation and admission cleanup.
